newsitem.title: UK: Euro fuel barges softer, straight-run sought after.
newsitem.headline: Euro fuel barges softer, straight-run sought after.

text.p: European fuel barges ignored crude's strength on Tuesday and lost value in thin business while straight-run material was eagerly sought, traders said.
One high sulphur barge traded at $86 fob ARA a tonne early before buying interest slipped back. Later deals were done at $85 and $84 fob.
"A lack of nominations and a lack of bunker demand is behind it," said one trader. "When you see crude is up $1 yesterday and fuel is coming down, then you realise this is a pretty sick market."
Traders said some of the weakness could be blamed on softer paper in Singapore, where much of last week's fuel oil strength originated.
One percent cargo markets were quiet, with little supply seen before end-month.
But low sulphur straight-run material was in high demand, since it gives very attractive refining margins compared to newly more expensive crude.
Two deals were seen yesterday, for 25,000 tonnes from Scandinavia at between $101 and $103 to a European major and for 30,000 tonnes from Antwerp to a U.S. refiner for $103 fob.
But sellers complained straight-run was still undervalued, given that crude has hit two-month highs, and saw further rises in price.
"I shall certainly be looking for more than $105 for my next cargo," said one seller.
